summary: Instagram is doing most of the work: nearly every Hindi video gets 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly stalls under 100 views. The best performers are the 'X doesn't see/hear, it only senses Y' videos about relatable robots and sensors (gyro robot, clap switch, PIR motion sensor), which also earn the most likes and saves. Videos with generic 'How does X work?' titles about everyday places (lift, tap, mall door, smoke alarm) and the one English video get very little attention.
winningPattern: Hindi Instagram Reels about hands-on maker subjects (robots, clap switch, PIR, mic, line follower) with a surprising 'it doesn't do what you think' hook, such as 'Without X this robot falls instantly' or 'It doesn't hear claps, only noise'. Titles are short Hinglish with one emoji and a strong curiosity or contradiction in the first words. Robot and clap-switch topics lead; these videos were posted in the Oct 26 to Nov 5 window and also got the best YouTube numbers (400-680 views).
doMore: Make more robot and Arduino-module videos built on a surprising contradiction hook ('X can't see, only Y').
Do follow-ups to the clap switch and gyro robot hits, e.g. whistle, noise, and failure demos (part 2 / 'what if' versions).
Lead with Instagram, then post to YouTube Shorts using the same Hinglish title style that worked for the top videos.
Show a visible build or a failure on screen (robot falling, switch triggering wrongly) rather than a plain explanation.
Ask viewers to save/share in the closing line, since shares and saves are strong on the robot IR video (10 shares) and gyro video (12 saves).
stopDoing: Stop making generic 'Kaise Pata Chalta Hai?' videos on everyday installations (lift, mall door, street light, taps), which get under 600 views.
Stop posting English-narrated videos and near-duplicate topics (three smoke/IR/tap variants) in the same week; they split attention and underperform.
Stop publishing to YouTube only: the last two uploads have zero Instagram views.
